scope: P0 field-priority scan with China/Xuzhou public evidence
purpose: Find low-permission, low-cost reality probes where state change creates underused resources on one side and blocked outcomes on another, without preselecting an industry or product.
seed_lenses_not_ontology: time surplus <-> task or structure deficit
digital/AI execution surplus <-> real-world problem/trust deficit
fragmented available time <-> asynchronous bounded task deficit
idle local asset surplus <-> route-to-market deficit

prefer: real actors can be reached through ordinary lawful channels
first decisive facts are observable without proprietary data
no enterprise procurement is required for the first probe
no large capital is required for the first probe
the state change and resource underuse can be observed before pitching a solution
existing routes can be checked quickly and the hypothesis can die cheaply
defer_for_p0: requires NDA or internal enterprise systems before learning anything decisive
requires data-rights negotiation before observing the underlying resource
requires procurement or a pre-existing contract
requires founder to build software before field truth
requires capital deployment to learn whether the gradient exists

actors: new/recent retirees or other experienced people leaving a full-time organizational role
formation_labs.state_change: retirement can abruptly remove the organization that previously converted experience, relationships and judgment into daily use; students simultaneously gain powerful AI/digital execution while still lacking real-world context, trust and problem access
formation_labs.potential_gradient: experienced judgment, time and social context on one side; fast digital execution, learning capacity and AI leverage on the other
existing_exchange_counterevidence: Silver Engineer / retired high-skill flexible-service programs already exist
older-adult AI learning and digital-assistance programs already exist
student entrepreneurship, internship and enterprise-project channels already exist
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: After subtracting those existing routes, are there recurring outcomes that experienced people want without returning to employment and that young executors cannot reach without domain judgment/trust, where a new bounded exchange would make both states better?
formation_labs.first_probe: separate opt-in conversations with 5 experienced transition actors and 5 students; map state change, currently underused resources, repeated desired outcomes, current workarounds and rejected routes before proposing any pairing
kill_conditions: no repeated underuse after the transition
no complementary blocked outcome appears across multiple actors
existing employment/expert/student-project routes already solve the same outcome adequately
value requires one side to become a disguised employee or cheap labor

actors: small shops/community spaces with recurring off-peak idle capacity
residents/creators/retired teachers/hobby experts with a callable skill
nearby people seeking low-commitment activities or social connection
formation_labs.state_change: urban spaces and community facilities increasingly have measurable periods of underuse while more residents seek nearby low-cost learning, hobby and social activity
formation_labs.potential_gradient: idle physical capacity + callable local skill + unmet nearby activity/time-slot demand
existing_exchange_counterevidence: community shared-space and resident-host models already exist
commercial venue rental and event platforms already exist
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: Are there hyperlocal time slots where the owner values foot traffic/activation more than rent, a local host has underused skill, and residents want a tiny recurring outcome that existing venue/class routes are too expensive or formal to organize?
formation_labs.first_probe: observe 5 nearby spaces at two off-peak windows and separately talk to 5 potential local hosts; no lease, renovation or event launch before repeated idle-time and host/outcome evidence appears
kill_conditions: space is not actually idle
owners require normal commercial rent that removes surplus
existing community/commercial activity already satisfies the same outcome
coordination or liability cost exceeds the value

actors: small local merchants / tiny organizations with bounded unresolved operational problems
students/young people seeking real projects and evidence of capability
formation_labs.state_change: AI lowers execution cost and makes smaller tasks technically solvable while students increasingly have tools but lack authentic problems; many tiny actors still have tasks too small or ambiguous for formal agencies
formation_labs.potential_gradient: real problem access/trust on one side + low-cost modern execution on the other
existing_exchange_counterevidence: student enterprise practice and OPC programs already exist
freelance and agency markets already sell small-business digital services
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: Do recurring micro-problems exist that are below agency economic thresholds yet sufficiently real and bounded to create valuable proof for students without making them free labor?
formation_labs.first_probe: collect 10 recent problems from reachable small actors using only problem/outcome/current-workaround/deadline fields; independently ask 10 students which exact task classes they can evidence and accept under bounded conditions
kill_conditions: problems are generic services already cheaply solved on existing platforms
business owners only want unpaid labor
tasks cannot be bounded or objectively accepted
student capability cannot be evidenced

actors: caregivers / stay-at-home parents / others with fragmented but recurring available time
formation_labs.state_change: care responsibilities can remove contiguous work hours while leaving fragmented time and prior skills available
formation_labs.potential_gradient: fragmented recurring time and skills <-> work that can be decomposed asynchronously
existing_exchange_counterevidence: community flexible-employment programs already match caregivers to local microjobs
data labeling, customer service, content moderation and remote flexible jobs already exist
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: Is there a higher-value bounded task class that existing flexible-employment channels systematically fail to expose because they over-index on low-skill piecework?
formation_labs.first_probe: research only; do not promote until a repeated task class and actor-side skill evidence appear beyond existing flexible-job supply
kill_conditions: existing flexible-work routes already serve the same task/value level
only low-value piecework remains
coordination around fragmented time destroys task economics

actors: return-home young people with outside-market/digital capability
households/villages/local operators with underused spaces, products, knowledge or relationships
formation_labs.state_change: some young people return with digital and external-market knowledge while local physical/cultural/production assets remain underused or poorly connected to demand
existing_exchange_counterevidence: national and local policy already explicitly promotes return-home entrepreneurship and idle-asset activation
many incubators and rural entrepreneurship parks already organize this exchange
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: At household or micro-community scale, are there assets too small or irregular for formal incubators but still able to support a low-cost new exchange?
formation_labs.first_probe: only scan specific reachable assets and current non-use reasons; do not infer opportunity from the existence of rural idle assets
kill_conditions: formal programs already activate the same asset
asset use requires heavy permits/capital
route-to-market cost exceeds incremental value

actors: residents with underused non-sensitive skills or organizing ability
formation_labs.state_change: community governance and shared-space programs are increasingly exposing resident skills and micro-needs that were previously private and disconnected
formation_labs.potential_gradient: trusted local attention + resident capability + tiny recurring outcomes
existing_exchange_counterevidence: community host, volunteer and shared-living-room models already exist
formation_labs.missing_edge_question: Which useful resident capabilities remain uncallable because volunteering and commercial services are both the wrong commitment level?
formation_labs.first_probe: observe one community or residential cluster and record only recurring requests, resident-offered skills and current coordination failures; no resident profiling
kill_conditions: volunteer/community programs already close the same edge
no repeat outcome exists
trust/safety requirements make lightweight orchestration inappropriate

current_p0_decision.deprioritized_reason: The hypothesis may still be real, but its first decisive truth requires higher permission, data-rights and enterprise access than the accessible human/community formation labs. Keep it as backlog evidence, not current P0.
